title: Colombe's Birthday: A Play
author: Robert Browning
blurb: A play in five acts. On her birthday Colombe, Duchess of Juliers and Cleves, learns that her right to the duchy is disputed by her cousin Prince Berthold; her courtiers desert her, and only the poor advocate Valence, who has come to plead for his town, stays true. The question is whether she will keep a crown or find a love.

title: The Columbiad
subtitle: A Poem in Ten Books
author: Joel Barlow
blurb: Barlow's patriotic epic on the American Republic: the imprisoned Columbus is shown, in vision, the history and future of the New World by the genius Hesper, in ten books of heroic couplets.

title: The Comedy of Errors
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Two sets of identical twins, the sons of the Syracusan merchant Egeon and their twin servants, separated by shipwreck in infancy, are drawn into the same day in Ephesus. Mistaken for one another by wives, friends, a goldsmith and a courtesan, they bring on beatings, arrests and a supposed madness, until the Abbess who shelters one of them proves to be Egeon's long-lost wife, and the family is reunited.

title: Comus
subtitle: A Mask Presented at Ludlow Castle
author: John Milton
blurb: A masque of chastity and temptation, performed at Ludlow Castle in 1634 — a Lady lost in the wood and the enchanter Comus.

title: Conary
author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse retelling of the destruction of the hostel of Da-Derga and the death of King Conary Mor.

title: Confessio Amantis
subtitle: Tales of the Seven Deadly Sins
author: John Gower
blurb: A lover confesses to Venus's priest Genius, who works through the Seven Deadly Sins with a great gathering of exemplary tales — classical, biblical, and romance — in eight books of octosyllabic couplets.

title: Congal
subtitle: A Poem in Five Books
author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
blurb: Ferguson's five-book heroic poem of Congal Claen, King of Ulster, and the battle of Moira (Moyra) in the seventh century.

title: The Conquest of Canaan
subtitle: A Poem, in Eleven Books
author: Timothy Dwight
blurb: Timothy Dwight's biblical epic in eleven books, the first American epic poem, follows Joshua's campaigns against Ai, Gibeon and the Canaanite kings in heroic couplets, with the love of the young warrior Irad and the maiden Selima woven through the war and a prophetic vision of later history in Book X.

title: Constance
subtitle: or, The Portrait
author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
blurb: A narrative poem in five parts, in heroic couplets, of love and fate begun in a portrait and played out on an English country estate.

title: The Tragedy of Coriolanus
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Caius Martius, the proudest soldier in Rome, wins the name Coriolanus by taking the Volscian city of Corioles, but his contempt for the common people makes him unfit for the consulship he is pressed to seek. Tricked and banished by the tribunes Sicinius and Brutus, he goes over to his old enemy Tullus Aufidius and marches on Rome at the head of a Volscian army. Only the pleading of his mother Volumnia, his wife Virgilia and his son turns him back, and the peace he makes costs him his life at Aufidius's hands.

title: Count Basil
subtitle: A Tragedy
author: Joanna Baillie
blurb: Count Basil, a young general in the Emperour's service, is kept at Mantua by his love for Victoria, the Duke's daughter, while the Duke and his minister Gauriceio plot to turn his troops against him. Basil wins the mutinous soldiers back, but when the Imperial army wins the battle of Pavia without him he can bear the shame no longer and shoots himself in a cave, dying in his friend Rosinberg's arms. This is the tragedy of love in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

title: Count Julian: A Tragedy
author: Walter Savage Landor
blurb: Count Julian, the Spanish governor who has brought the Moors into Spain to avenge the dishonour of his daughter Covilla by King Roderigo, finds that his vengeance has delivered his country to the invaders. Landor's blank-verse tragedy follows Julian between the Moorish princes Muza and Abdalazis, the repentant Roderigo and the bishop Opas, as the cost of his revenge falls on his family and on Spain.

title: The Countess Cathleen
author: W. B. Yeats
blurb: In an Irish famine of old times, two demons disguised as merchants buy the starving peasants' souls for gold. The young Countess Cathleen sells her own soul to ransom theirs, while the poet Aleel, who loves her, looks on in anguish. Yeats's first long verse play moves from the peasants' hut to her great hall and back, and ends with a vision of the soul's pardon.

title: The Course of Time
subtitle: A Poem, in Ten Books
author: Robert Pollok
blurb: Robert Pollok's blank-verse epic in ten books, in which a bard of Paradise tells a newly arrived spirit the history of mankind from the Creation to the Last Judgement; published months before the young Scottish poet's death, it went through many editions.

title: The Courtship of Miles Standish
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
blurb: Longfellow's hexameter tale of the Plymouth Colony, in which Miles Standish sends the young John Alden to woo Priscilla Mullins for him, and she asks why he does not speak for himself.

sections.title: V. The Sailing of the May Flower
VII. The March of Miles Standish

title: The Curse of Kehama
author: Robert Southey
blurb: A Hindu mythological epic in twenty-four sections, in irregular rhymed stanzas: the Rajah Kehama curses the peasant Ladurlad, who is drawn into a pursuit that reaches the Swerga and the hell of Padalon.

title: The History of the Wars of Alexander
subtitle: Books III–X, translated by John Digby, 1714
author: Quintus Curtius Rufus
blurb: Curtius's Latin history of Alexander the Great, from the war in Asia Minor after the Granicus to the king's death at Babylon and the division of his empire (the first two books and several passages are lost), in John Digby's English of 1714.

title: The Cyclops
author: Euripides
blurb: Odysseus, landing on Sicily, bargains with the old satyr Silenus for food and wine, only to fall into the hands of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. The only complete satyr play to survive, here in Coleridge's literal prose.

title: The Cyclops
subtitle: A Satyric Drama
author: Euripides
blurb: Odysseus and his men, landing on Sicily, bargain with the old satyr Silenus for food and wine, only to fall into the hands of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. Euripides' only surviving satyr play, the lone complete example of the genre, is rendered by Shelley in 1819 and was first printed after his death.

title: The Tragedie of Cymbeline
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Cymbeline, king of Britain, banishes his daughter Imogen's secret husband Posthumus Leonatus. Tricked by the Italian Iachimo into believing her unfaithful, Posthumus orders her death; she flees in boy's disguise to Wales, where she finds her two long-lost brothers, and the play's tangled threads of war with Rome, the Queen's poison and a divine vision resolve in reconciliation. It includes the songs 'Hark, hark! the lark' and 'Fear no more the heat o' the sun'.

title: Cynegetica
subtitle: The Chase
author: Oppian
blurb: A didactic poem in four books on hunting: the hunter, his horses and hounds, and the wild beasts of the chase, addressed to the emperor Caracalla.

title: The Dance to Death
subtitle: A Historical Tragedy in Five Acts
author: Emma Lazarus
blurb: Nordhausen, May 1349: as the Black Death spreads, the Jews of the free city are accused of poisoning the wells. Susskind von Orb, a respected Jew, sees his daughter Liebhaid loved by Prince William of Meissen, while the vengeful Governor Henry Schnetzen, whose wife was once burned through Susskind, secures the Landgrave's order for their destruction. Lazarus's verse tragedy, dedicated to George Eliot, ends with the community choosing a martyr's dance of death.

title: Daniel
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: A verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

title: Daniel (Old English)
subtitle: Old English text
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

title: Dante at Verona
author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
blurb: Rossetti's narrative poem of Dante in exile at the court of Can Grande, torn between the Florence that cast him out and the Beatrice he lost.

title: The Economy of Vegetation
subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part I
author: Erasmus Darwin
blurb: Darwin's four-canto didactic poem in heroic couplets, in which Nymphs of Fire, Gnomes, Nymphs of Water and Sylphs preside over the natural philosophy of heat, earth, water and air.

title: The Loves of the Plants
subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part II
author: Erasmus Darwin
blurb: Darwin's four-canto poem in heroic couplets, in which the botanic Muse presents the Linnaean sexual system of plants as a comedy of courtships, marriages and rivalries among flowers.

title: The Daughters of Troy
subtitle: The Trojan Women
author: Euripides
blurb: Troy has fallen. In the Greek camp the captive women of the royal house wait to be shared out among the victors: Hecuba is given to Odysseus, the prophetess Kassandra to Agamemnon, and Andromache to Akhilleus' son. Their one remaining hope is taken from them when the Greeks decide to hurl Hector's little son from the walls, and the play ends as the city burns and the captives are driven down to the ships.

title: Davideis
subtitle: A Sacred Poem of the Troubles of David
author: Abraham Cowley
blurb: Cowley's unfinished biblical epic in rhymed couplets, telling of David's youth and his persecution by King Saul, in four books.

title: The Dawn in Britain
subtitle: In twenty-four books
author: Charles M. Doughty
blurb: Doughty's blank-verse epic of Britain from the first settlement to the Roman conquest, told in twenty-four books in a deliberately archaic, Spenserian English.

title: De Monfort
subtitle: A Tragedy
author: Joanna Baillie
blurb: De Monfort, a proud German nobleman, is eaten up by hatred of Rezenvelt, a rival whose easy fortune and ready praise he cannot forgive. His sister Jane tries to reconcile them, but a false report that Rezenvelt means to marry her drives him past endurance, and he murders his enemy in a wood near a convent. Taken by the monks, he dies of remorse in his sister's arms. This is the tragedy of hatred in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

title: The Death of Wallenstein
author: Friedrich Schiller
blurb: Wallenstein, dismissed by the Emperor and urged by his officers toward revolt, hesitates between the stars and his own ambition and opens talks with the Swedes. Max Piccolomini chooses duty over love, and dies in battle; Thekla follows him in grief; at Egra Wallenstein is murdered by his own officers.

title: The Deformed Transformed
subtitle: A Drama
author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
blurb: Byron's unfinished drama, dated Pisa, 1822, and first published in 1824, of which only two parts and the opening chorus of a third were completed. The hunchback Arnold, scorned by his mother, accepts from a mysterious Stranger a new and beautiful body, and with the Stranger, who takes the form of his former shape, joins the army of the Constable Bourbon at the sack of Rome in 1527. Byron's advertisement names an old novel, The Three Brothers, and Goethe's Faust as sources.

title: Deirdre
subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse drama of the flight, return and death of Deirdre and the sons of Usnach, set between Glen Etive and the House of the Red Branch at Emania.

title: Deirdre
author: W. B. Yeats
blurb: Fergus brings Naisi and Deirdre back to Ireland from exile, on the promise of King Conchubar's pardon. Waiting in a guest-house in a wood, while musicians sing and hint at treachery, the lovers learn that Conchubar means to take Deirdre for himself. The tragedy of the old Irish tale ends in a trap, a death, and a queen's last choice.

title: The Demon
author: Mikhail Lermontov
blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

title: The Demon
author: Mikhail Lermontov
blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

title: On the Chersonese (Or. VIII)
subtitle: Diopeithes and the Chersonese, 341 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes defends the general Diopeithes and urges Athens to resist Philip in the Chersonese.

title: On the Crown (Or. XVIII)
subtitle: The speech in reply to Aeschines, 330 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes' defence of his public career against Aeschines' attack on the proposal to crown him.

title: On the Embassy (Or. XIX)
subtitle: Against Aeschines on the false embassy, 343 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes' prosecution of Aeschines for misconduct as an ambassador to Philip.

title: The First Olynthiac (Or. I)
subtitle: Help for Olynthus, 349 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: The first of three speeches urging Athens to send help to Olynthus against Philip.

title: The First Philippic (Or. IV)
subtitle: The first speech against Philip of Macedon, 351 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes' first attack on Philip of Macedon, calling on the Athenians to raise a proper citizen force.

title: For the Megalopolitans (Or. XVI)
subtitle: Athens and the Arcadian city, c. 353 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes argues that Athens should support Megalopolis against Sparta while keeping Thebes weak.

title: On the Naval Boards (Or. XIV)
subtitle: The Athenian navy and the Persian threat, 354 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes' first public speech, urging Athens not to rush into war with Persia and proposing a reform of the Boards that equipped the fleet.

title: On the Peace (Or. V)
subtitle: The Peace of Philocrates, 346 BC
author: Demosthenes

blurb: Demosthenes urges the Athenians to help the Rhodian democrats against a Carian-backed oligarchy.

subtitle: Philip and the Peace, 344 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes warns the Athenians against Philip's intrigues in the Peloponnese.

author: Demosthenes
blurb: The third Olynthiac, urging military aid for Olynthus and the reform of the Theoric Fund.

title: The Third Philippic (Or. IX)
subtitle: The call to resist Philip, 341 BC
author: Demosthenes
blurb: Demosthenes' call for Athens to rouse the Greek states against Philip.

title: The Didache, or Teaching of the Twelve Apostles
subtitle: The Lord's teaching to the heathen by the Twelve Apostles
author: The Apostolic Fathers
blurb: An anonymous early Christian church manual, rediscovered in 1873, setting out the Two Ways, rules for baptism, fasting, the Eucharist and church order.

subtitle: Volume I: Books I–V and XI–XIV, with Booth's translation of 1700 as reprinted in 1814
author: Diodorus Siculus
blurb: Diodorus Siculus's universal history, from the myths and marvels of Egypt, Asia and early Greece to the Greek affairs of the fourth century BC, in George Booth's English prose (volume I).

title: The Historical Library, Volume II: Books XV–XX and Fragments
subtitle: Volume II: Books XV–XX and the fragments of the lost books
author: Diodorus Siculus
blurb: Diodorus Siculus's history of Greece, Sicily and the wars of Alexander's successors (Books XV–XX), with the fragments of the later books, in George Booth's English prose (volume II).

title: Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Books I–X
subtitle: Diogenes Laertius, lives, sayings and doctrines of the Greek philosophers from Thales to Epicurus
author: Diogenes Laertius
blurb: The chief ancient source for the lives, sayings and doctrines of the Greek philosophers, from the Seven Sages and the Ionians through Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and the Cynics and Stoics to Pythagoras, the Sceptics and Epicurus, in R. D. Hicks's complete English of 1925, in ten books.

title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books I–V
subtitle: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Greek philosophers from Thales to Heraclides of Pontus
author: Diogenes Laertius
blurb: The chief ancient source for the lives and sayings of the Greek philosophers, from the Seven Wise Men through Socrates, Plato and the Academy to Aristotle and his school, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books VI–X
subtitle: Antisthenes and Diogenes through Epicurus
author: Diogenes Laertius
blurb: Laertius's lives of the Cynics, Stoics, Pythagoreans, Eleatics, Sceptics and Epicurus, with the three letters and the maxims of Epicurus, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

title: The Divine Comedy
subtitle: La Divina Commedia
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: Cary's blank-verse version of the Commedia, the standard English Dante of the nineteenth century, rendered canto by canto in Miltonic pentameter.

title: The Divine Comedy
subtitle: La Divina Commedia
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: Dante's vision of the afterlife in a hundred cantos, from the dark wood through Inferno and Purgatorio to the Paradiso, in Longfellow's blank-verse tercets.

title: The Divine Comedy (Norton)
subtitle: Translated by Charles Eliot Norton
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: A literal, unrhymed prose version of the Commedia by the Harvard scholar Charles Eliot Norton, long valued by students for its fidelity to Dante's sense; each canto opens with a brief summary of its argument.

title: The Divine Comedy (Plumptre)
subtitle: Translated by E. H. Plumptre
author: Dante Alighieri
translator: trans. E. H. Plumptre (1886–87; text of the Isbister edition, 1899)
blurb: The Commedia in English terza rima by Edward Hayes Plumptre, Dean of Wells, keeping Dante's three-line stanzas and line count; each cantica was published with extensive notes, which are omitted here.

title: Christus: A Mystery. Part I: The Divine Tragedy
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
blurb: The first part of Longfellow's trilogy Christus: A Mystery, a dramatic poem on the life of Christ. After an Introitus in which an Angel carries the prophet Habakkuk to Babylon, three Passovers follow the Gospel story from John the Baptist's preaching and the temptation in the wilderness through the miracles, the raising of Lazarus, the Last Supper, trial and Crucifixion, to the appearances after the Resurrection. The Epilogue gives the Apostles' Creed, spoken line by line by the Twelve. Part II is The Golden Legend.

title: Domesday Book
author: Edgar Lee Masters
blurb: A verse narrative in blank verse that opens with a coroner's inquest into the death of Elenor Murray, a nurse found dead by the Illinois River. Witness after witness is called, and each account lays bare the hidden lives of a Midwestern town and of America.

title: Don Juan
author: Lord Byron
blurb: Byron's unfinished comic epic in ottava rima follows a young Spaniard through seductions, shipwreck, war and the courts of Europe, mocking cant, politics and poetry itself along the way.

title: The Dream of Gerontius
author: John Henry Newman
blurb: Newman's dramatic poem of a dying man's passage through death and judgment, in seven parts: the prayers at the deathbed, the soul's journey with its guardian Angel, the Demons, the choirs of Angelicals, and the soul's entry into Purgatory.

title: The Dreaming of the Bones
subtitle: A play for dancers
author: W. B. Yeats
blurb: In the aftermath of the Easter Rising of 1916, a young man fleeing from the Dublin fighting meets two strangers among the ruins of Corcomroe Abbey in County Clare. They are the ghosts of Dermot and Dervorgilla, whose adultery brought the Norman invasion to Ireland seven hundred years before, and they ask for his forgiveness.

title: The Duchess of Malfi
author: John Webster
blurb: The widowed Duchess of Malfi secretly marries her steward Antonio against the commands of her brothers, the violent Duke Ferdinand and the scheming Cardinal. Their spy Bosola uncovers the marriage, and the brothers imprison, torment and finally strangle her, along with her children and her maid. Bosola, sickened by the deed, turns on his masters, and the play ends in a bloodbath of revenge and ruin.

title: The Dynasts: Part First
subtitle: A Drama of the Napoleonic Wars
author: Thomas Hardy
blurb: Hardy's vast panorama of the Napoleonic Wars, from the threat of invasion in 1805 to Austerlitz. Above the earthly action the Spirits of the Years and the Pities watch the workings of the unconscious Immanent Will, in choruses of lyric verse.

title: The Earthly Paradise
subtitle: Parts II–IV: May to February
author: William Morris
blurb: Morris's frame story of wanderers who, seeking an earthly paradise, settle in a western city whose elders swap classical and medieval tales with them month by month. Part II holds the tales of Cupid and Psyche, Alcestis, the Son of Croesus, Pygmalion and Ogier the Dane. Parts III and IV add the autumn and winter tales: the Death of Paris, the Land East of the Sun and West of the Moon, Acontius and Cydippe, the Man who never Laughed Again, Rhodope, the Lovers of Gudrun, the Golden Apples, Aslaug, Bellerophon, the Ring given to Venus and the Hill of Venus.

sections.title: The Story of Cupid and Psyche
The Land East of the Sun and West of the Moon
The Story of Acontius and Cydippe
The Man who never Laughed Again

title: The Earthly Paradise
subtitle: Part I: The Prologue, March and April
author: William Morris
blurb: Morris's frame story of Norse wanderers who sail in search of the earthly paradise and end their days in a western city whose elders trade tales with them month by month. Part I holds the Apology (‘the idle singer of an empty day’), the Prologue in which the wanderers tell their own story, and the tales of March and April: Atalanta's Race, the Man Born to be King, the Doom of King Acrisius and the Proud King.

sections.title: The Man Born to be King

title: Ecclesiastes
subtitle: Authorized Version of Ecclesiastes.
author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
blurb: The reflections of the Preacher on vanity, time and the limits of human wisdom.

title: The Troublesome Reign and Lamentable Death of Edward the Second
author: Christopher Marlowe
blurb: Edward II, newly king, recalls his favourite Gaveston from exile and showers him with titles, driving the barons under the younger Mortimer into open revolt. After Gaveston is killed and the king turns to the Spensers, Queen Isabella and Mortimer invade, depose Edward and have him murdered in Berkeley Castle. His son, the young Edward III, then brings Mortimer to the block.

title: Egyptian Tales, First Series
subtitle: Translated from the Papyri, IVth to XIIth Dynasty
author: Ancient Egyptian (anonymous)
blurb: Four of the oldest stories in the world: the magicians at the court of Khufu, the eloquent peasant, the shipwrecked sailor and the exile of Sanehat, translated from the papyri.

title: Egyptian Tales, Second Series
subtitle: Translated from the Papyri, XVIIIth to XIXth Dynasty
author: Ancient Egyptian (anonymous)
blurb: Four tales from the New Kingdom papyri: the stratagem by which Tahutia took Joppa, the prince doomed to crocodile, serpent or dog, the quarrel of the brothers Anpu and Bata, and Setna's theft of the magic book of Thoth.

title: Electra
author: Sophocles
blurb: Orestes returns to Mycenae in disguise, sent by Apollo to avenge Agamemnon. Electra, who has mourned her murdered father for years, believes her brother dead until he reveals himself; together they kill their mother Clytemnestra and then her lover Aegisthus.

title: Electra
author: Sophocles
blurb: Years after Agamemnon's murder, his daughter Electra still keeps vigil at the palace gates of Mycenae, scorned by her mother Clytaemnestra and her mother's lover Aegisthus. Her brother Orestes returns in secret with a false tale of his own death, and the siblings' recognition scene turns grief into revenge. Jebb's plain English prose carries the play's cold fury and its choral laments.

title: Electra
author: Euripides
blurb: In a poor peasant's cottage on the borders of Argos, Agamemnon's daughter Electra waits in squalor for her exiled brother Orestes to return and avenge their father on Klytemnestra and Aegisthus. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of recognition and vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

title: Elene
author: Cynewulf
blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena, mother of the Emperor Constantine, and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, opening with Constantine's vision of the Cross before his battle at the Milvian Bridge.

title: Elene (Old English)
subtitle: Old English text
author: Cynewulf
blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, in the original Old English.

title: Emare
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
blurb: Emare, daughter of the emperor Artyus, wears a marvellous robe embroidered with famous lovers; when her father conceives a sinful passion for her she is set adrift in a boat and comes ashore in Galys, where the king marries her. His mother's lies drive Emare and her child into exile at sea again, until a penitent pilgrimage to Rome reunites the whole family.

title: The Emigrants
subtitle: A Poem in Two Books
author: Charlotte Smith
blurb: Charlotte Smith's blank-verse meditation on the French Revolution and the refugee clergy and nobility who fled to the Sussex coast, set against her own grief and the English countryside.

title: The Fragments of Empedocles
subtitle: Translated into English verse
author: Empedocles
blurb: The surviving fragments of Empedocles' two hexameter poems, On Nature and The Purifications, in William Ellery Leonard's English verse: the four roots, Love and Strife, the cycles of the cosmos, and the wandering of the soul.

sections.title: Last Echoes of a Song Half Lost

title: Empedocles on Etna
subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
author: Matthew Arnold
blurb: On the slopes of Mount Etna, the young harp-player Callicles and the physician Pausanias attend the philosopher Empedocles, who is exiled, weary of men and of his own restless thought. Callicles sings of the gods and of Chiron's teaching of Akhilleus, Pausanias hopes to cure his friend, and Empedocles on the summit, in a long meditation on mind, desire and the unity of things, leaps into the crater, while Callicles' song rises from below.

title: Endymion
subtitle: A Poetic Romance
author: John Keats
blurb: Keats's four-book retelling of the myth of the shepherd prince Endymion, loved by the moon goddess and wandering the earth, sea and underworld in search of her.

title: The Seven Tablets of Creation
subtitle: Enuma Elish
author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
blurb: The Babylonian epic of creation, in which the god Marduk slays the sea-goddess Tiamat, fashions the world from her body, and receives his fifty names.

title: The Epic of Hades
subtitle: In Three Books
author: Sir Lewis Morris
blurb: A Victorian dream-vision in three books: the poet walks through Tartarus, Hades and Olympus, hearing the shades of Greek myth tell their own stories and the gods reveal what they stand for.

title: The Epic Songs of Russia
subtitle: The Byliny of the Kiev and Novgorod Cycles
author: Anonymous (Russian Byliny)
blurb: The great heroic songs of the Russian north: Ilya of Murom and the Nightingale the Robber, Dobrynya the Dragon-slayer, Sadko beneath the sea, and the champions who defend Prince Vladimir's Kiev.

title: The Works of Epictetus: Discourses, Enchiridion and Fragments
author: Epictetus
blurb: The lectures of the Stoic teacher Epictetus as recorded by his pupil Arrian, with the Enchiridion, or Manual, and the surviving fragments, in Thomas Wentworth Higginson’s revision of Elizabeth Carter’s translation.

title: The Discourses of Epictetus
subtitle: with the Encheiridion and Fragments
author: Epictetus
blurb: The lectures of the Stoic teacher Epictetus as recorded by his pupil Arrian, with the Encheiridion, or Manual, and the surviving fragments, in George Long’s translation.

title: The Epigoniad
subtitle: A Poem in Nine Books
author: William Wilkie
blurb: An epic in nine books on the war of the Epigoni, the sons of the Seven, against Thebes, in heroic couplets modelled on the Iliad.

title: The Epistle of Barnabas
subtitle: Traditionally ascribed to Barnabas
author: The Apostolic Fathers
blurb: An anonymous early Christian letter of c. AD 100–130, long ascribed to Barnabas, the companion of Paul, urging a spiritual reading of the Hebrew scriptures and setting out the Two Ways.

title: The Epistle to Diognetus
subtitle: An early Christian apologetic letter
author: The Apostolic Fathers
blurb: An anonymous Greek apologetic letter to a certain Diognetus, setting out why Christians reject pagan idols and Jewish observance, how they live in the world as the soul does in the body, and what the revelation of the Son means.

title: Erec and Enide
subtitle: Erec et Enide
author: Chrétien de Troyes
blurb: The first Arthurian romance in French verse, telling how Erec wins Enide and then must prove himself again.

title: Erechtheus
subtitle: A Tragedy
author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
blurb: A tragedy on the Greek model. Athens is besieged by Eumolpus and his Thracians, and an oracle demands that King Erechtheus sacrifice one of his daughters to save the city. Swinburne's choruses sing of Athens, the sea and the sun, and the play ends with Athena's promise of the city's glory.

title: The Erle of Tolous
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
blurb: A tail-rhyme Breton lay of about 1,220 lines: Barnard, earl of Tolous, defeats the emperor Dyaclysyon, wins a sight of the empress Beulybon through the knight Trylabas, and later, disguised as a monk, takes up her cause when two knights falsely accuse her. After the emperor's death he becomes emperor and marries her.

title: Eros and Psyche
subtitle: A narrative poem in twelve measures
author: Robert Bridges
blurb: Bridges's narrative poem of Psyche and Eros, drawn from the story in Apuleius and told in seven-line stanzas across the twelve months of the year, from Psyche's earthly parentage in the spring to her reception into heaven in the winter.

title: An Essay on Man
subtitle: In Four Epistles to Henry St John, Lord Bolingbroke
author: Alexander Pope
blurb: Pope’s attempt, in polished couplets, to ‘vindicate the ways of God to Man’ — four epistles on man’s place in the universe, himself, society, and happiness.

title: Eugene Onéguine
subtitle: A Romance of Russian Life in Verse
author: Alexander Pushkin
blurb: Pushkin's verse novel of the bored St Petersburg dandy Onegin, the provincial girl Tatiana who loves him, and the duel that kills his friend Lensky.

title: Europe: A Prophecy
author: William Blake
blurb: Enitharmon's eighteen-hundred-year sleep, the reign of Urizen's law over Europe, and the coming of the revolutionary fire of Orc.

title: Europe
subtitle: Lines on the War
author: Reginald Heber
blurb: Heber's verses of 1809 on the war against Napoleon, opening in a grove at Dresden and ending in hope for Spain.

title: Evangeline
subtitle: A Tale of Acadie
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
blurb: A story of a young Acadian woman who is separated from her promised husband when their people are driven from their homes, and who spends her whole life searching for him.

title: Everyman
subtitle: The Summoning of Everyman
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
blurb: God, displeased that mankind has forgotten him in worldly prosperity, sends Death to summon Everyman to a reckoning. Abandoned in turn by Fellowship, Kindred and Goods, and later by Beauty, Strength, Discretion and Five-Wits, Everyman is accompanied to the grave only by Good-Deeds. The best-known English morality play, in rhyming verse of the late fifteenth century.

title: The Pontic Epistles
subtitle: Ovid's Letters from the Black Sea, Books I–IV, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
author: Ovid
blurb: Ovid's four books of verse epistles from exile, each addressed by name to a friend or patron in Rome, pleading for help and describing life among the Getae, in Riley's prose.

title: Exodus
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: A dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

title: Exodus (Old English)
subtitle: Old English text
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

title: The Faerie Queene
subtitle: Books I–VI, with the Mutabilitie Cantos
author: Edmund Spenser
blurb: Spenser's vast allegorical epic of knights, virtues, and the Faerie court — six completed Books (Holinesse, Temperaunce, Chastitie, Friendship, Iustice, Courtesie) plus the fragmentary Mutabilitie Cantos, in the original 1590s spelling.

title: The Fairy Godmother-in-Law
author: Oliver Herford
blurb: A comic sequel to Cinderella, in which the Prince and Princess are visited by her fairy godmother, who proves an even more formidable relation than the average mother-in-law.

title: The Fall of Robespierre
subtitle: An Historic Drama
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
blurb: A three-act historical drama on the overthrow of Robespierre in July 1794, published at Cambridge in 1794 as a pamphlet under Coleridge's name. In the first act Tallien, Legendre and Barrere plot against the dictator; in the second he is denounced in the Convention and led off under arrest; the third follows the aftermath of his rescue by Henriot. The first act is Coleridge's; the second and third are Southey's.

title: The Fall of Troy
subtitle: Posthomerica
author: Quintus Smyrnaeus
blurb: Quintus Smyrnaeus continues the Iliad from the funeral of Hector through the deaths of Akhilleus, Paris and the Amazon queen Penthesileia, the wooden horse and the sack of Troy, to the Greeks' storm-wrecked voyage home.

title: The Farmer's Boy
subtitle: A Rural Poem
author: Robert Bloomfield
blurb: A rural poem in four seasons, following the labours and pleasures of a farm boy through the year.

title: The Fasti
subtitle: Ovid's Roman Calendar, Books I–VI, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
author: Ovid
blurb: Ovid's poem on the Roman festival calendar, here in Riley's prose: the six surviving books, January to June, with the rites, myths and star-risings of each month.

title: The Fates of the Apostles
author: Cynewulf
blurb: A brief martyrology recounting, in turn, the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing the Vercelli Book poem with Cynewulf's runic signature.

title: The Fates of the Apostles (Old English)
subtitle: Old English text
author: Cynewulf
blurb: A brief martyrology recounting the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing with Cynewulf's runic signature, in the original Old English.

title: Faust: The First Part
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: Dr. Heinrich Faust, a scholar sick of the limits of human knowledge, is wagered over in Heaven and then bargains his soul to the devil Mephistopheles in return for a moment of fulfilment. Mephistopheles draws him through the tavern, the witches' kitchen and a Walpurgis-Night revel, and into a love affair with the young Margaret, whose mother, brother and child are destroyed in its wake. Margaret, imprisoned for infanticide and awaiting execution, refuses Faust's offer of escape and gives herself up to God; a voice from above declares her saved.

sections.title: Walpurgis-Night's Dream (Oberon and Titania's Golden Wedding)

title: Faust: The Second Part
subtitle: Translated in the original metres by Bayard Taylor
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: The Second Part of Goethe's Faust in Bayard Taylor's translation in the original metres: Faust serves the Emperor's court, follows Helen of Troy through the Classical Walpurgis-Night to a marriage that ends with the death of their son Euphorion, wins land from the sea, and dies at the hour his own labour is complete, as the angels carry off what is immortal in him.

title: The Feast of Bacchus
subtitle: A Comedy in the Latin manner, partly translated from Terence
author: Robert Bridges
blurb: Bridges's comedy in the Latin manner, privately printed at Oxford in 1889 and published in 1894, partly translated from Terence. The action takes place in a single day in a suburb of Athens, on the feast of Bacchus, among the households of Menedemus and Chremes.

title: Fifine at the Fair
author: Robert Browning
blurb: Don Juan's long, teasing defence of inconstancy to his wife Elvire at a Breton fair, framed by the Prologue "Amphibian" and the Epilogue "The Householder".

title: Fingal: An Ancient Epic Poem
subtitle: In Six Books
author: James Macpherson
blurb: Ossian's epic of Fingal's rescue of Ireland from Swaran, king of Lochlin, in measured prose.

title: The Fleece
subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
author: John Dyer
blurb: Dyer's didactic poem in four books of blank verse on the English wool trade, from the care of sheep and the shearing to the loom, the markets and the ships that carry cloth to the world.

title: Floris and Blauncheflur
subtitle: Middle English text of the Trentham manuscript, ed. J. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
author: Anonymous
blurb: A Middle English romance of two children, the Christian Blauncheflur and the king's son Floris, who are raised together and then parted when his father sells her to merchants; Floris sets out for Babylon and wins her back from the Emir's tower.

title: The Foray of Queen Meave
subtitle: Five Fragments of an Ancient Irish Epic (The Táin Bó Cuailgne)
author: Aubrey de Vere
blurb: De Vere’s blank-verse retelling, in five fragments with a prologue, of the Táin Bó Cuailgne: Queen Meave of Connacht invades Ulster for the Brown Bull, and the young Cuchullain holds the ford alone.

sections.title: Fragment I: The Cause of the Great War
Fragment II: The Deeds of Cuchullain
Fragment III: The Combat at the Ford
Fragment IV: The Invasion of Uladh

title: The Forest Sanctuary
author: Felicia Hemans
blurb: A Spanish Protestant, fleeing religious persecution in the sixteenth century, tells his story from a North American forest where he has taken refuge with his child.

title: Fragments of Psalms (Old English)
subtitle: Metrical psalm passages from the Benedictine Office: Old English text
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: Short passages of Old English verse translation from twenty-five psalms, found in the Benedictine Office.

title: The French Revolution
author: William Blake
blurb: Blake's unfinished poem on the fall of the Bastille; only the first of its seven projected books was printed, in 1791.

title: Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
subtitle: The Honourable History of Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
author: Robert Greene
blurb: Prince Edward, hunting near Fressingfield, falls in love with Margaret, the Keeper's daughter, and sends Lacy, Earl of Lincoln, to woo her on his behalf; Lacy falls for her himself. Meanwhile Friar Bacon of Oxford, a scholar of magic, builds a brazen head to wall England in brass, defeats the German conjurer Vandermast in a contest of spirits, and shows Edward the distant courtship in a glass. The play ends with Edward's renunciation of Margaret, her marriage to Lacy, and Bacon's prophecy at a royal wedding.

title: Fridthjof's Saga
subtitle: A Norse Romance
author: Esaias Tegnér
translator: trans. Thomas A. E. Holcomb and Martha A. Lyon Holcomb (1876)
blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Fridthjof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in English verse by the Holcombs.

subtitle: Frithiof's Saga
author: Esaias Tegnér
blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Frithiof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in the English verse of Captain Spalding, a second translation, in the original measures, of 1872.

title: The Furies
subtitle: The Oresteia
author: Aeschylus
blurb: Pursued by the Furies of his murdered mother, Orestes flees to Apollo's shrine at Delphi and then to Athens. Athena sets up a jury of Athenian citizens to try him; the votes tie, and her own vote acquits him. She persuades the angry Furies to stay in Athens as the kindly Eumenides, honoured guardians of the city.

title: Gammer Gurton's Needle
author: William Stevenson (attributed)
blurb: Gammer Gurton loses the needle with which she was mending her servant Hodge's breeches, and the mischievous vagabond Diccon the Bedlam persuades her that her neighbour Dame Chat has stolen it. Accusations, a brawl and the arrival of the curate, Doctor Rat, and the bailiff follow, until Hodge, struck by Diccon, finds the needle sticking in his own breeches. One of the earliest English comedies, it opens Act II with the drinking song 'Back and side go bare, go bare'.

title: The Dispensary
subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
author: Sir Samuel Garth
blurb: A mock-heroic satire on the apothecaries who opposed the College of Physicians' free dispensary for the poor, told as an epic battle of drugs, doctors and allegorical spirits. Text of the first edition (London, 1699), with its original spelling.

title: The Gathas of Zarathustra
subtitle: Yasna 28–34, 43–51 and 53, from the Zend-Avesta, Part III
author: The Avesta
blurb: The seventeen hymns of the Gathas, the oldest layer of the Avesta and traditionally ascribed to Zarathustra himself, in L. H. Mills’s prose translation of 1887.

title: Gebir
author: Walter Savage Landor
blurb: Landor's first major poem, a blank-verse epic in seven books. Gebir, prince of Spain, invades Egypt and falls in love with its young queen Charoba, while his brother Tamar loves her sister Dalica. Magic, an underworld descent and a fatal gift of poisoned robes follow.

title: Genesis
subtitle: Genesis A and Genesis B
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: A verse paraphrase of Genesis running from the Creation and the fall of the rebel angels through Abraham and the near-sacrifice of Isaac, opening the Junius Manuscript.

title: The Story of Genesis and Exodus
subtitle: Middle English biblical verse paraphrase, ed. Richard Morris (EETS, 1865)
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
blurb: An East Midland verse paraphrase of about 4,160 short couplet lines, written about 1250, that retells the Book of Genesis and the first part of Exodus from the Creation and the Fall of Lucifer to the death of Moses, with much borrowed legend and commentary.

The Exodus and the Red Sea
Balaam and the Death of Moses

title: Genesis (Old English)
subtitle: Old English text
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a verse paraphrase of Genesis running from the Creation and the fall of the rebel angels through Abraham and the near-sacrifice of Isaac, opening the Junius Manuscript.

title: The Gentle Shepherd: A Pastoral Comedy
author: Allan Ramsay
blurb: Set in a Lowland village in the years after the Restoration, Ramsay's pastoral follows Patie, a shepherd who loves Peggy, a foundling he takes for a poor girl, while his friend Roger woos Jenny and the dull Bauldy plots against them. Sir William Worthy, the exiled laird, returns in disguise and the secret of Peggy's birth comes out, so that the lovers may marry. The play is built of Scots dialogue in couplets, with twenty-one songs set to old tunes.

title: The Georgics
subtitle: Dryden's heroic-couplet translation
author: Virgil
blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in Dryden's heroic couplets: tillage and the weather, the vine and olive, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

title: The Georgics
subtitle: Fairclough's prose translation
author: Virgil
blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in H. Rushton Fairclough's plain prose: tillage and the weather, the vine and olive, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

title: The Georgics
subtitle: Prose translation
author: Virgil
translator: trans. J. W. Mackail (1889; Longmans reprint 1910)
blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life, in J. W. Mackail's prose: the work of the fields and the weather, trees and vines, cattle and horses, and the keeping of bees.

title: The Georgics
subtitle: Blank-verse translation
author: Virgil
blurb: Virgil's Latin poem in four books on farming and country life: the tilling of fields, the vine and olive, the rearing of cattle, and the keeping of bees.

title: Germany: A Winter Tale
subtitle: Deutschland. Ein Wintermärchen
author: Heinrich Heine
blurb: Heine's satirical verse journey home from exile in Paris to Hamburg in twenty-seven cantos, mocking Prussian authority and German nationalism.

title: The Ghost
author: Charles Churchill
blurb: Churchill's rambling octosyllabic satire in four books, begun as an attack on the Cock Lane ghost hoax and growing into a gallery of attacks on Johnson, Mansfield and Warburton.

title: Gil Perez, the Gallician
author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
blurb: FitzGerald's free version of Calderón's play on a notorious Spanish robber, whose name he changes to Gil. A farmer of Galicia, Gil falls out with the law and takes to the hills; the play follows him through Portugal and Andalusia to a confrontation with the Judge and a final pardon.

title: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
subtitle: The Pennsylvania and Yale Tablets
author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
translator: trans. Morris Jastrow Jr. and Albert T. Clay (1920)
blurb: Gilgamesh's dreams of Enkidu, the wild man's taming and their wrestling meeting in Erech, and the pair's plan to go against the monster Humbaba in the cedar forest.

title: The Epic of Gilgamish
subtitle: Verse translation from the Assyrian and Babylonian tablets
author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
blurb: The Babylonian epic of Gilgamish, king of Erech, and his friend Enkidu, who together slay the Ogre Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven, until Enkidu's death sends the hero in vain search of everlasting life.

sections.title: Tablet I: Of the Tyranny of Gilgamish, and the Creation of Enkidu

Tablet X: How Gilgamish Reached Uta-Napishtim

title: The Indian Song of Songs (Gita Govinda)
author: Jayadeva
blurb: Jayadeva's twelfth-century Sanskrit song cycle of Krishna and Radha, in Sir Edwin Arnold's English verse: a hymn to Vishnu and eleven sargas of longing, quarrel and union.

Sarga the Eleventh: The Union of Radha and Krishna

title: The Glory of the Nightingales
subtitle: A Poem
author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
blurb: Blank-verse narrative in six parts: Malory, bent on revenge, travels from Sharon to the seaside mansion of his old rival Nightingale, with the memory of Agatha, whom both loved, driving the story.

title: The Athenaid
subtitle: A Poem
author: Richard Glover
blurb: Glover's posthumous blank-verse epic in thirty books, a sequel to Leonidas that sets Athens against the Persian Empire of Xerxes.

title: Leonidas
subtitle: A Poem
author: Richard Glover
blurb: Glover's blank-verse epic of Leonidas and the three hundred at Thermopylae, in nine books, a patriotic favourite of its day.

title: The Gods of the North
subtitle: An Epic Poem
author: Adam Oehlenschläger
blurb: Oehlenschläger's cycle of thirty cantos retelling the Norse myths, chiefly the adventures of Thor and the mischief of Lok, among the Aesir and the giants, in Frye's English rhymed and blank verse.

title: The Golden Legend
subtitle: Christus: A Mystery, Part II
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
blurb: A dramatic poem set in medieval Germany, drawn from Hartmann von Aue's tale of Poor Henry. Prince Henry of Hoheneck, wasting with a mysterious sickness, is told that only a maiden's willing death can cure him. Elsie, a peasant girl, offers hers, and the two travel through Strasburg, the Black Forest convent of Hirschau, the Alps and Italy to the medical school at Salerno, where Henry prevents the sacrifice. Lucifer in disguise tempts the travellers throughout, and a Miracle Play of the Nativity is performed inside the Strasburg scenes. Longfellow made the poem the second part of his trilogy Christus: A Mystery.

sections.title: Prologue: The Spire of Strasburg Cathedral

title: Gondibert
subtitle: An Heroick Poem
author: Sir William Davenant
blurb: Davenant’s unfinished heroic poem in decasyllabic quatrains — three books and twenty cantos of love, war and statecraft among the Lombards.

title: The Greater Testament
subtitle: Le Testament, translated by John Payne
author: François Villon
blurb: Begun about 1461, after Villon's release from prison at Meung, this long mock will mingles confession, satire and lament, and holds the ballads on which his fame mostly rests, among them the Ballad of Old-Time Ladies.

title: The Green Helmet
subtitle: An Heroic Farce
author: W. B. Yeats
blurb: Cuchulain returns from Scotland to find Laegaire and Conall refusing to honour his claim as the champion, while a Red Man from the sea comes to collect an old debt: a beheading game agreed a year before. In rhymed fourteeners, Yeats turns the Irish tale of Bricriu's Feast into a comic-heroic farce, ending in a gesture of reckless generosity.

title: Greenfield Hill
subtitle: A Poem, in Seven Parts
author: Timothy Dwight
blurb: Dwight's seven-part descriptive and patriotic poem on the Connecticut village where he was minister, from its rural prospect and the burning of Fairfield to a vision of America's future.

sections.title: Part III. The Burning of Fairfield
Part IV. The Destruction of the Pequods
Part V. The Clergyman's Advice to the Villagers

title: Gudrun
subtitle: A Mediaeval Epic
author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
blurb: The Middle High German epic of Kudrun, the Hegeling princess abducted by Hartmut and held captive for thirteen years until her kin come to win her back, in thirty-two tales of four-line stanzas, rendered into English verse by Mary Pickering Nichols.

title: Guidone and Lucia
author: Walter Savage Landor
blurb: A narrative poem in rhymed couplets, set among the Guelph and Ghibelline feuds of Italy, of the lovers Guidone and Lucia.

title: Gunlaug
author: Walter Savage Landor
blurb: A narrative poem in rhymed couplets on the Icelandic poet Gunlaug, his love for Helga, and his quarrel and duel with his friend Rafen.

title: Guthlac
subtitle: Guthlac A and Guthlac B
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: The life of St. Guthlac of Crowland, a former warrior turned hermit who does battle with demons in the Lincolnshire fens (Guthlac A), and an account, closely based on Felix's Latin Life, of his final illness and death (Guthlac B).

title: Guthlac (Old English)
subtitle: Guthlac A and Guthlac B: Old English text
author: Anonymous (Old English)
blurb: The Old English verse of the life of St. Guthlac of Crowland, a former warrior turned hermit who does battle with demons in the Lincolnshire fens (Guthlac A), and an account of his final illness and death (Guthlac B).

title: Halieutica
subtitle: On Fishing
author: Oppian
blurb: A didactic poem in five books on the natures, habits and capture of sea creatures, addressed to the emperors Marcus Aurelius and Commodus.

title: The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Prince Hamlet, summoned home to Elsinore by his father's death, is told by the Ghost that Claudius, now king and married to Hamlet's mother, murdered him. Feigning madness and staging a play to catch the king's conscience, Hamlet delays his revenge while the court around him unravels: Polonius is killed, Ophelia is driven to drowning, and Laertes returns for vengeance. The final duel leaves almost the whole court dead and the throne to Fortinbras of Norway.

title: The Code of Hammurabi
subtitle: The Oldest Code of Laws in the World
author: Hammurabi
blurb: The best-known law code of ancient Mesopotamia, issued by the king of Babylon c. 1750 BC: laws on theft, land, trade, marriage, injury and the hire of labour.

title: Harold: A Drama
author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
blurb: Tennyson's verse drama of the last Saxon king. Harold, Earl of Wessex, is shipwrecked on the Norman coast and forced to swear an oath to Duke William, a vow that haunts him when the dying Edward the Confessor names him heir. Crowned king, he defeats his brother Tostig and the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge, then marches south to meet the Normans at Hastings, where he falls and Edith finds his body on the field of the dead.

title: Harold the Dauntless
subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
author: Sir Walter Scott
blurb: A verse romance of the Danish settlement of Northumbria: the fierce heathen Harold, son of Count Witikind, is drawn through blood, magic and a warning from the grave toward repentance and the love of the Danish maid Eivir.

title: The Lay of Havelok the Dane
subtitle: Middle English verse romance, ed. W. W. Skeat (EETS, 1868)
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
blurb: An English verse romance of about 3,000 lines in which Havelok, the dispossessed son of a Danish king, is raised by a fisherman, marries the English princess Goldeborw, and wins back both kingdoms.

title: Heaven and Earth
subtitle: A Mystery
author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
blurb: Byron's biblical drama on the eve of the Flood, begun at Ravenna in October 1821 and first published in The Liberal in 1823. Anah and Aholibamah, descendants of Cain, are loved by the angels Samiasa and Azaziel, while the patriarch Noah's son Japhet loves Anah. As the waters rise, the angels carry the two women away and Japhet is left on a rock as the Ark floats towards him. Only the first part of the work was written.

title: Hecuba
author: Euripides
blurb: After the fall of Troy, the captive queen Hecuba loses her daughter Polyxena to sacrifice at the tomb of Akhilleus, then finds the body of her youngest son Polydorus, murdered for his gold by the Thracian king who was sheltering him. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of grief turned to vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

title: Helen of Troy
author: Andrew Lang
blurb: Lang's retelling of the story of Helen in six books of rhyme royal, from the coming of Paris to Sparta to the sack of Troy and the return of Helen to Menelaus, with Helen conceived as the unwilling victim of the gods.

sections.title: Book I: The Coming of Paris
Book II: The Spell of Aphrodite
Book III: The Flight of Helen
Book IV: The Death of Corythus
Book VI: The Sack of Troy. The Return of Helen

title: Helen
author: Euripides
blurb: Euripides follows the Recantation of Stesichorus: the Helen who went to Troy was only a phantom of cloud, while the true Helen waited in Egypt, chaste, at the tomb of King Proteus. When shipwrecked Menelaus arrives, husband and wife must trick the king who wishes to marry her. Arthur Way renders this romantic tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

title: The Ethiopics; or, Adventures of Theagenes and Chariclea
subtitle: Smith translation, 1855
author: Heliodorus of Emesa
blurb: The Greek romance of the lovers Theagenes and Chariclea, parted by pirates, priests and kings from Delphi to Egypt and Ethiopia: the best-known ancient novel, in Rowland Smith's English prose of 1855.

title: Hellas
subtitle: A Lyrical Drama
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
blurb: Shelley's lyrical drama of the Greek War of Independence, set in the Sultan's Constantinople, closing with the chorus 'The world's great age begins anew'.

title: The Henriade
subtitle: An epic poem in ten cantos
author: Voltaire
translator: trans. Tobias Smollett, Thomas Francklin and others (1762)
blurb: Voltaire's epic of Henri IV and the French Wars of Religion, from the St Bartholomew massacre to the siege and surrender of Paris.

title: The First Part of King Henry the Fourth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: The Percy family, who helped Henry IV to the throne, rise against him, led by the fiery Hotspur. Meanwhile the king's son, Prince Hal, wastes his days in Eastcheap taverns with the fat knight Sir John Falstaff and his thieving companions. Hal at last turns to honour, takes up arms for his father, and kills Hotspur at the battle of Shrewsbury.

title: The Second Part of King Henry the Fourth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: The Archbishop of York and his allies rise in a second rebellion, and Prince John of Lancaster crushes it at Gaultree Forest by a false promise of peace and a prompt arrest. Falstaff, sent recruiting into Gloucestershire, trades old memories with Justice Shallow and takes bribes from the men he chooses to spare. Meanwhile the dying king, troubled by a crown that has cost him sleep, makes his peace with Prince Hal, who on his accession rejects Falstaff in the street.

title: Henry the Leper (Der Arme Heinrich)
subtitle: A Swabian Miracle-Rhyme
author: Hartmann von Aue
blurb: Hartmann's tale of a nobleman struck with leprosy and the peasant girl who offers her life for his cure, in Rossetti's rhymed paraphrase.

title: The Life of King Henry the Fifth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Henry V presses his claim to the throne of France, exposes the traitors Cambridge, Scroop and Grey at Southampton, takes Harfleur, and wins against heavy odds at Agincourt, with the Chorus asking the audience to supply what the stage cannot show. The war ends in the comic, halting wooing of Katherine of France.

title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: The play opens at the funeral of Henry V, as the English hold France only by the valour of Talbot, whom Joan la Pucelle and the French confront at Orleans and beyond. In the Temple Garden the red and white roses are plucked, and the quarrel of York and Lancaster begins. Suffolk, meanwhile, woos Margaret of Anjou on the young king's behalf, with designs of his own.

title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Henry VI's marriage to Margaret of Anjou opens a reign of faction: the Duchess of Gloucester's sorcery brings down the good Duke Humphrey, murdered at the instigation of Suffolk, who is himself killed at sea by pirates. Jack Cade's rabble rising sweeps London in prose and carnage, while Richard of York throws off his pretence and openly claims the crown, winning the first battle of St Albans and opening the Wars of the Roses.

title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Henry VI, weak and pious, disinherits his own son in favour of the Duke of York, setting the Wars of the Roses ablaze: York is taunted and slain at Wakefield, the king watches the carnage from a molehill at Towton, and Warwick the Kingmaker changes sides when Edward IV marries for love. Edward's victory at Tewkesbury closes the play, with Gloucester, the future Richard III, murdering the captive Henry in the Tower.

title: King Henry the Eighth
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Henry VIII's court sees the proud Duke of Buckingham brought down by Cardinal Wolsey's schemes, until Wolsey's own power turns to ruin when the king's eye falls on Anne Bullen. Queen Katherine defends her marriage at the Blackfriars trial and dies with dignity at Kimbolton. The play ends with the king's marriage to Anne and Cranmer's prophecy of greatness at the christening of the infant Elizabeth.

title: Hercules Furens
subtitle: Mad Hercules
author: Seneca
blurb: Juno, furious that Hercules has returned alive from the underworld, sends a madness upon him. While the tyrant Lycus presses Hercules’ wife Megara and old Amphitryon at the altar, the hero comes home, kills the usurper, and is then driven by Juno to slaughter his own wife and children, taking them for the family of his enemy Eurystheus. He wakes in his right mind to see what he has done, and only the entreaties of his friend Theseus keep him from suicide.

title: Hermann and Dorothea
subtitle: Hermann und Dorothea
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: A domestic epic in nine cantos of unrhymed hexameters: a German innkeeper's son falls in love with a refugee girl from the Rhine, against the backdrop of the French Revolution.

sections.title: V. Polyhymnia: The Citizen of the World

title: Hero and Leander
subtitle: Sestiads III–VI (Chapman's continuation of Marlowe)
author: George Chapman
blurb: Chapman's continuation of Marlowe's unfinished erotic epyllion, carrying the story of Hero and Leander from the lovers' first night to Leander's drowning in the Hellespont.

title: The Histories
subtitle: The History of Herodotus, in nine books, called by the names of the Muses
author: Herodotus
blurb: Herodotus's account of the rise of the Persian Empire and the Greek wars against it, in G. C. Macaulay's English prose of 1890.

title: The Catalogues of Women and Other Fragments
subtitle: Fragments of the Hesiodic poems, in prose translation
author: Hesiod
blurb: The surviving fragments of the poems ancient readers ascribed to Hesiod beyond the Theogony and Works and Days: the genealogical Catalogue of Women, the Great Eoiae, the Melampodia, the Aegimius and shorter pieces, mostly preserved as quotations by later writers.

sections.title: The Catalogues of Women and Eoiae

title: The Hind and the Panther
subtitle: A Poem, in Three Parts
author: John Dryden
blurb: A long allegorical fable in which the milk-white Hind (the Catholic Church) and the Panther (the Church of England) debate faith and politics after James II’s accession.

title: Hippolytus
author: Euripides
blurb: Aphrodite, scorned by the chaste huntsman Hippolytus, makes his stepmother Phaedra fall helplessly in love with him, and the secret destroys them both, in Edward P. Coleridge's plain prose version of Euripides' tragedy.

title: Hippolytus
author: Euripides
blurb: Aphrodite, scorned by the chaste huntsman Hippolytus, makes his stepmother Phaedra fall helplessly in love with him, and the secret destroys them both, in Arthur Way's rhymed English verse version of Euripides' tragedy.

title: Aelius
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Lucius Aelius Caesar, Hadrian's first choice of successor, adopted in AD 136 and dead before he could rule, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Antoninus Pius
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Antoninus Pius (AD 138-161), the gentle and prudent ruler who followed Hadrian, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Avidius Cassius
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Vulcacius Gallicanus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Avidius Cassius, the Syrian commander who rose against Marcus Aurelius in AD 175, in the Latin biography ascribed to Vulcacius Gallicanus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Antoninus Caracalla
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Caracalla (AD 211-217), who murdered his brother Geta and ruled alone, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Clodius Albinus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Clodius Albinus, governor of Britain, made Caesar by Severus and later crushed by him at Lugdunum in AD 197, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Commodus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Lampridius
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Commodus (AD 180-192), son of Marcus Aurelius, gladiator and tyrant, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Antoninus Diadumenianus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Diadumenianus, the young son of Macrinus, made his father's colleague and put to death with him in AD 218, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Didius Julianus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Didius Julianus, who bought the empire from the Praetorians in AD 193 and held it for sixty-six days, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Antoninus Elagabalus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Elagabalus (AD 218-222), the young priest of the Syrian sun-god, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Antoninus Geta
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The short Life of Geta, Caracalla's younger brother and co-heir, murdered soon after their father's death, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: The Three Gordians
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Lives of the three Gordians, the elder and younger Gordian proclaimed in Africa in AD 238 and the boy emperor Gordian III (reigned 238-244), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Hadrian
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Hadrian (AD 117-138), traveller, builder of the Wall and restless ruler of the whole empire, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Lucius Verus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Lucius Verus, joint emperor with Marcus Aurelius from AD 161 until his death in 169, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Opellius Macrinus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Opellius Macrinus, the praetorian prefect who succeeded the murdered Caracalla and reigned briefly (AD 217-218), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Marcus Aurelius
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the philosopher-emperor Marcus Aurelius (AD 161-180), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: The Two Maximini
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the soldier-emperor Maximinus and of his son and colleague Maximinus the Younger (AD 235-238), in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Maximus and Balbinus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Maximus (Pupienus) and Balbinus, the two senators raised to the purple in AD 238 against Maximinus, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: Pertinax
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Julius Capitolinus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Pertinax, the freedman's son who became emperor in AD 193 and was murdered within three months, in the Latin biography ascribed to Julius Capitolinus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Pescennius Niger
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of Pescennius Niger, the governor of Syria hailed emperor in the East in AD 193 and defeated by Severus, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Septimius Severus
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 1, by Aelius Spartianus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Septimius Severus (AD 193-211), the African soldier who won the civil war and founded a dynasty, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Spartianus, in David Magie's English translation of 1921.

title: Severus Alexander
subtitle: Historia Augusta, vol. 2, by Aelius Lampridius
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
blurb: The Life of the emperor Severus Alexander (AD 222-235), the longest in this volume and the most openly admiring, in the Latin biography ascribed to Aelius Lampridius, in David Magie's English translation of 1924.

title: H.M.S. Pinafore
subtitle: Or, The Lass That Loved a Sailor
author: W. S. Gilbert
blurb: Aboard H.M.S. Pinafore off Portsmouth, Captain Corcoran's daughter Josephine loves the humble sailor Ralph Rakestraw, while the Captain wants her to marry Sir Joseph Porter, First Lord of the Admiralty, who rose from office boy to rule the Queen's Navee. The lovers plan to elope, the villainous Dick Deadeye betrays them, and Little Buttercup's confession of a baby-swap long ago puts every rank in its right place.

title: The Homeric Hymns
author: Homer
blurb: Thirty-three anonymous hymns of invocation to the Greek gods, transmitted alongside Homer’s epics since antiquity and traditionally (though almost certainly wrongly) attributed to him.
